ASSUMPTION: Section 1 says "in neither did public-data software show a meaningful advantage" and "the campaign did not find a place where public-data software would create a meaningful Cubs advantage". Only two decisions were tested, and the R001 primary test never ran a model (early stop). The scope is "two tested decisions", not the campaign question in general. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r003

ASSUMPTION: "Both against pre-registered baselines" and "neither tool beat a simple rule" overstate R001. The pre-registered primary test stopped early with no model fitted and the 2025 holdout untouched. The model-vs-B0 comparison is exploratory, user-requested, "no claim". Presenting it as a FACT in "What the method establishes" promotes an exploratory result. CITE: assessment-r001

ASSUMPTION: "Both negatives held up under ... a holdout used once, and recounts from raw data" mixes the runs. R001's holdout was never used. R001's early-stop count was recounted from raw season files. For R003 the evidence shows a single 2026 evaluation, but the R3-S2 recount was a controller check of the defective artifact. The sentence should be split per run. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r003

ASSUMPTION: "The deciding public information was missing or too thin" is unfair for R001. R001's stated reason is a thin pool (12-23 positives, below the minimum of 30) and a ceiling of under one contributor per club. Nothing in assessment-r001 says that a particular piece of deciding information is missing. The scouting, health and makeup list in the synthesis is not in the evidence, so it is invented. The claim is supported only for R003 (play-level tracking), and even there it is an INFERENCE. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r003

ASSUMPTION: "Better modelling was not what was lacking" is not tested. R001 has no model result for the primary segment. R003 tested one reduced logistic model, and the full covariate set was unavailable (67 outs against the 140 required). R003 also notes that the full model could not be used, so the claim is not established. CITE: assessment-r003

ASSUMPTION: The synthesis's INFERENCE that MILBFA's "practical ceiling is small even with better data" conflicts with its own claim that better data would help. R001 says the ceiling is about one player a year in the low-attention segment only. The whole-pool segment, where players with MLB time sit, was not shown to be capped. The inference should be limited to the segment. CITE: assessment-r001

ASSUMPTION: "In both cases the evidence suggests where an advantage would have to come from" for MILBFA is unsupported. R001 only says that the segment is thin. IDEA: replace with "For R003, play-level tracking would be the deciding data (INFERENCE). R001 does not identify a missing data source."

ASSUMPTION: "Readable at 375 and 1280 px" in the delivered list is an overclaim. R005 meets its criteria as tested, but it lists an open item: at 375 px the send/hold estimate column wraps its prose into tall rows. R005 also claims no user value. IDEA: "layout tests and screenshot inspection at 375 and 1280 px pass; one minor wrapping issue is open." CITE: assessment-r005

ASSUMPTION: "Tests prove it reaches these values, layouts and keyboard paths" is too strong. R004 says the tests prove displayed numbers equal the source values, and R004 and R005 also found readability defects that escaped all tests. CITE: assessment-r004, assessment-r005

ASSUMPTION: "Failover carried every session" is not supported. R004 shows two sessions ended in HANDOFF, one session was discarded, and R004-S1 ended HANDOFF after every worker was excluded. R001 also had S1 and S2 stoppages. CITE: assessment-r004, assessment-r001

ASSUMPTION: "Claude, Codex, Cursor and AGY each finished work at some point" is supported only by R001's statement that all four served as workers. "Served" is not the same as "finished". For R004, AGY and Devin were "usually NO_REPOSITORY_CHANGE". CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r004

ASSUMPTION: "HANDOFF states stopped incomplete work from merging" and "Review and acceptance blocked bad work several times" have R001 support only. Elsewhere the evidence also shows false rejections (DOG-044: three rejections of a passing tree) and a controller-discard. Review effectiveness is mixed, and the synthesis presents the same tally of misses without noting the false rejections. CITE: findings-index, assessment-r004

ASSUMPTION: The Howl table says "Post-merge public proof is recorded for DOG-035 to 039 (R001)". Findings-index registers a post-merge proof file only for DOG-035. R001 says that all were merged with "post-merge public proof", but DOG-039's fix was merged in #166 after the R001 assessment, which gives one source and one conflict. Also, "Registry text on main still says FIX IN REVIEW" was noted for DOG-035 and is not mentioned. CONFLICT: dog035_registry_status. CITE: findings-index, assessment-r001, assessment-r002

ASSUMPTION: "All merged, with regression tests and HowlPlane review" for DOG-044 and DOG-035 to 039 is a single claim across ten defects. The DOG-044 entry in the index lacks an explicit review reference, though it was made by session 03d1d55e and CI fixed by d516f2a9. DOG-037/038's review ended COMPLETE WITH WARNINGS, which the synthesis leaves out. CITE: findings-index

ASSUMPTION: "Proof of fixes" claims: DOG-041 and DOG-042 are not live-proven, and the synthesis says so, which is fair. But it describes DOG-040's proof as live, whereas the R002 proof was one session on one scenario. That is bounded evidence, not a general proof. CITE: assessment-r002

CONFLICT: calls_per_run_and_hours. The synthesis states R003 "33 of 40" Dream calls. Assessment-r003 says 27 of 40. R001 34 of 40 matches. The synthesis also says R004 used spec critique and two prompt-review rounds with no counts, while R003's own count covers passes 1, 2, 4 plus the challenge. CITE: assessment-r003

CONFLICT: prompt_lessons_count. "v1 to v4 added 18 operating lessons in section 19A" has no support. R004 lists seven lessons for v4, R003 four candidates for v3, and R001 only says v2 adopted. No total of 18 appears. CITE: assessment-r003, assessment-r004

R001 gives the league-wide segment counts as 2018 20, 2019 12, 2021 14, 2022 12, 2023 22, 2024 23. ASSUMPTION: "Even perfect selection there would have added about one player a year" is described in R001 as "roughly one", and it assumes the Cubs could have signed those players. R001 states that availability and terms are unknown. The synthesis repeats that caveat, which is fair, but the sentence should say "roughly". CITE: assessment-r001

ASSUMPTION: The synthesis dates (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-11) and "Cubs' 2026 season ended on 2026-09-30" are unsupported by the supplied evidence. UNKNOWN: cubs_2026_season_end_date

ASSUMPTION: "In-game ideas parked" and "MiLB promotion timing converged in 5 of 6 trials in R003 pass 4" come from OPPORTUNITIES.md, which was not supplied. R001 gives the 4 of 6 recurrence of minor-league free agency. These are not checkable. UNKNOWN: opportunities_md_contents

ASSUMPTION: Missing or misrepresented section 19 items:
- Baseball: no mention of "why it mattered" for the SENDHOLD decision, nor of the strong alternatives for R003 beyond the first-pass candidates.
- Limits on data that would improve the work. R001 names WAR and projection systems that are not lawfully bulk-accessible. The synthesis does not carry these over.
- R001 limitations omitted: the outcome measures playing time (opportunity as well as talent), and the two methods for separating minor-league elections disagree (~15%).
- Durability: no exact resume instructions, no per-repository commit/PR/check table, no push or local-only state, no help requests and user responses, no manifest fields (clean/dirty, upstream, modified-by-mission).
- Campaign state is not stated (ACTIVE versus PAUSED_NEEDS_HELP). The synthesis recommends stopping or asking without recording the state.
- Per-run outcome and delivery states are omitted, apart from R001 and R003 outcomes. R002 COMPLETE_REGRESSION and R004 and R005 COMPLETE_USEFUL are missing from the answer table.
CITE: prompt-s19

ASSUMPTION: R003 delivery is misstated. Assessment-r003 says PRs #7, #8 and #9 were PR_OPEN awaiting the user's merge. The synthesis says "All earlier run PRs are merged" and lists cubs-edge-lab main as 97901d2. R004 says later PRs were merged, so a later merge may have occurred, but it is not evidenced in the supplied records. UNKNOWN: r003_pr_merge_status. CITE: assessment-r003, assessment-r004

ASSUMPTION: R004 and R005 deviations are partly dropped. The synthesis lists R004's deviations but omits R003's pre-registration amendment (v3, approved by the owner after the freeze but before fitting). It also does not note that R004's session discard broke the rule in v3 section 19A. R003's mislabel (AMBIGUOUS) correction is not carried over. CITE: assessment-r003, assessment-r004

ASSUMPTION: The "repeated practical use unproven for every artifact" line is correct for R001. R003 does not state a repeated-use verdict, which makes the generalisation reasonable but unsourced for the Cubs send/hold analysis. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r003

ASSUMPTION: The autonomy list includes "repair authorizations (DOG-035, DOG-044)". R001 says there were three repair authorizations, so the list is incomplete. "Every merge from R003 on" is also unsupported: R005 says that the merge was by the controller at the owner's explicit request, which is in line with the synthesis, but R002's merge (howlplane #167) is not shown to have been by the owner. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r005

ASSUMPTION: The recommendation to stop or pause is only partly justified. Section 19 allows a pause when no meaningful next experiment exists. But the synthesis itself lists a credible public-data option that it dismisses: the MILBFA confirmatory test on the untouched 2025 holdout, which R001 describes as available for one pre-registered test given a new feature hypothesis. R001 also says that a new discovery using the unused pivot remains open. Also, with the "no hypothesis yet" gap, the supported conclusion is "no credible next experiment identified with the current hypotheses", not "none exists". CITE: assessment-r001, prompt-s19

ASSUMPTION: "Strongest next opportunity: SENDHOLD with tracking data" violates the stated data policy, so it is a request for an owner decision rather than a campaign experiment. Option 4, Howl-only regression work, is inconsistent with the Cubs question and section 19's rule that regression runs must have a justified purpose and make no baseball claim. It should be labelled as such. CITE: prompt-s19

ASSUMPTION: Other credible public-data follow-ups were overlooked or not examined:
- A FOLLOW_UP on the R001 whole-pool segment, where players with MLB time are, since the obvious rule matched the model only exploratorily.
- A FOLLOW_UP re-examining R003's "AMBIGUOUS" labelling, or a hold-side counterfactual using the full 2025-2026 retrieval already on disk, which costs no extra requests.
- Evaluation of the R003 sensitivity model with a larger out count (for instance pooling seasons) to reach the 140-out threshold. This would test whether the full covariate set changes the verdict, and it does not need new data.
Each is speculative and untested. The synthesis should say that these were considered, rather than state that none is credible. CITE: assessment-r001, assessment-r003

IDEA: Replace the "Short answer" with: "Two public-data decisions were tested. R001's pre-registered test stopped early because the segment was too thin (12-23 positives per year against the minimum of 30), and an exploratory whole-pool comparison roughly tied a simple rule. R003's pre-registered model did not beat a constant on the 2026 holdout, and the full covariate set was not reached. No public-data advantage was demonstrated; whether missing information explains it is an INFERENCE for R003 only."

IDEA: Replace the recommendation with: "No credible next public-data experiment was identified from the supplied evidence. Candidates considered: a MILBFA confirmatory test on the 2025 holdout (needs a new feature hypothesis), and an R003 reanalysis with pooled seasons. Pause and ask for direction (PAUSED_NEEDS_HELP)."

## Baseball

**Problem discovered.** HowlDream (passes 1, 2, 4; critique and blind-spot pass) moved discovery away from analyst dashboards toward offseason decisions. Minor-league free agency recurred in 4 of 6 second-pass trials: every November several hundred players elect free agency and clubs decide quickly, with limited scouting attention, whom to sign or invite.

**Alternatives and selection.** S1 measured public-data feasibility for three finalists. Rule 5 was rejected (explicit codes only from 2024). Call-up translation was rejected for this run (in-season, survivorship bias, strong public projections). MILBFA was selected: measurable pools (585-908 per offseason), public next-season outcomes, a named decision owner. Prior Cubs experiments (repertoire alerts, Wrigley wind, ABS) were excluded as explored families.

**Software built** (cubs-edge-lab, all through HowlPlane): a rate-limited Stats API probe with a content-free manifest; cohort construction with decision-time features (2018-2025 cohorts); outcome labels; baselines B0 (prior MLB time), B1 (level + rate stat), B2 (3-feature logistic), P (persistence) and model M; rolling-origin and validation evaluation with paired bootstrap; a pre-registration guard on the 2025 holdout; an exploratory whole-pool evaluation; a descriptive Cubs case. Bulk responses stay local under MLBAM's non-bulk terms.

**Design and evaluation.** Design v1 was written before any outcome label; the HowlDream challenge (pass 5) led to v2: stronger baselines, primary test in the low-attention segment (no MLB appearance in season Y), bootstrap and rolling-origin success rule, k = 50 fixed from measured Cubs signing volume (median 41) before any outcome, and an early-stop rule.

**Results.**
- Primary (pre-registered): early stop. In the no-MLB-in-Y segment, players reaching >=50 MLB PA or >=20 IP the next season: 2018 20, 2019 12, 2021 14, 2022 12, 2023 22, 2024 (validation) 23, below the minimum of 30. No model was fitted for the primary test; the 2025 holdout is untouched. Independently recounted from raw season files.
- Exploratory (whole pool, user-requested, no claim): model M roughly ties B0, the "played in MLB last year" ranking: top-50 hits 43/41, 48/44, 41/43, 38/32 (2021-2024); 2024 AUROC difference -0.016 (95% -0.049 to 0.014).
- Practical significance: the low-attention pool holds about 12-23 next-season contributors per year league-wide, under one per club. A ranking tool has little hidden value to find there, and where value is larger (players with MLB time) the obvious rule already finds it.

**Cubs application (dated, descriptive).** November-pool players the Cubs signed: 2021 14, 2022 12, 2023 10, 2024 8; of these, 3, 1, 6 and 0 reached the threshold next season. In the no-MLB-in-Y segment the Cubs had 1, 0, 1, 0 of 14, 12, 22, 23 league-wide positives. This establishes only the size of the opportunity: even perfect selection in that segment would have added roughly one player per year. It does not evaluate the Cubs' decisions (availability, terms, competing offers, roster needs are unknown).

**Limitations.** The outcome measures playing time, which reflects opportunity as well as talent; no public value metric (WAR) in this source; no comparison with projection systems (not lawfully bulk-accessible); thin samples per segment; two methods to separate minor-league from MLB elections disagree (~15%), sidestepped by using the whole pool.

**Repeated practical use:** unproven. **Rejected ideas** and evidence: OPPORTUNITIES.md. **Strongest next opportunity:** a FOLLOW_UP on MILBFA only with a genuinely new feature hypothesis (the 2025 holdout remains available for one pre-registered confirmatory test), or a new discovery using the unused pivot.

## Howl

**Components used.** HowlDream: 6 remote exploration passes (divergent, critique, second divergent, selection challenge, three prompt-review rounds; 34 of 40 calls; all remote Claude, mocked=false). HowlPlane: 15 orchestration sessions on cubs-edge-lab and on howlplane repair worktrees (planning, implementation, verification, independent review, rework, acceptance). Codex, Claude, Cursor and AGY all served as workers; Devin did not. HowlCreate, HowlWriter, HowlFrame, HowlProof, HowlForge: not used (no distinct role for them in this workload).

**Integration strengths.** Falsifying reviews caught real defects every time (stale reports, unsupported claims, an incomplete pipeline, missing planning coverage); bounded rework and HANDOFF states stopped bad work from merging; failover handled timeouts, quota limits and permission denials.

**Findings and repairs (all merged with regression tests, HowlPlane review and post-merge public proof).**
- DOG-035: `--verify` rejected commands with flags, including howl's README example (howlplane #164, howl #16).
- DOG-036: fixed, undocumented 300 s verification timeout (#164, `--verify-timeout`).
- DOG-037: AGY's read-only roles were not enforced; a reviewer rewrote research files and a verified implementation was lost (#165).
- DOG-038: no supported way to give workers network access for public data (#165, `--worker-network`).
- DOG-039: a Codex usage limit was recorded as "not authenticated" (#166).

**Open.** CUBS-P-002 (a refused test command marks a proven agent interactive-only everywhere); CUBS-P-003 (acceptance shown a superseded planner VERIFY_COMMAND); CUBS-P-008 (declared INCOMPLETE recorded as success); NOTE-005 (Dream validate does not warn on budget sizing); NOTE-006 (exported units carry pooled assumptions); NOTE-007 (flaky hygiene test); NOTE-008 (usage refusal reported as INTERNAL_ERROR); acceptance applying criteria outside the goal (observed twice). External: Claude and Codex session/usage limits (handled by failover).

**Local-LLM compliance.** LOCAL_LLM_USED: NO. HOWL_FORBID_LOCAL_INFERENCE=1 on every invocation; all Dream calls remote (manifests); all HowlPlane workers remote vendor CLIs.

**Limits on autonomy claims.** Several steps needed the user: repository visibility, three repair authorizations, a data-terms decision, two session-bound increases, a history rewrite, and two acceptance decisions. Controller interventions were outside product code: goals, constraints, discards, audits and merges.

The campaign did not find a place where public-data software would create a meaningful Cubs advantage. Its evidence suggests where an advantage would have to come from instead.

- On public MLB Stats API data, with these baselines and holdouts, neither tool beat a simple rule.
- Both negatives held up under pre-registration and early-stop rules, a holdout used once, and recounts from raw data.

- SENDHOLD: the Cubs had 157 send opportunities in 2025 and 159 in 2026. Their flagged holds carry the same uninterpretable "runs left" caveat.
